images.title: Times 99 is times 100 minus once
images.composition: One stacked column subtraction centred, with a short note above it. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: At the top, the label '9734 × 99', and beside it in reddish purple (#CC79A7) the label '99 = 100 − 1'. Below, a right aligned column subtraction in large dark digits: first row '973400', second row '− 9734' in vermilion (#D55E00), a horizontal rule, and the answer row '963666' in teal (#0072B2). Exactly 3 number rows.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: To multiply by 99, take a hundred times the number and subtract the number once.

image_decisions.why: Writing 99 as 100 − 1 is the whole trick; the subtraction layout shows it in one step.
